name: Chalk
author: E. T. Carter
description: A slate chalkboard mid-lesson: hand-drawn circles, triangles, hatch bundles and spirals chalked up stroke by stroke in white and palette-tinted pastel, with a dusty broken edge where the chalk catches the tooth of the slate. Each area is drawn, held, then wiped by an eraser pass that leaves a streaky dust ghost of the old marks, fading as the next set goes up. Dark stone ground with mottle, pits and a soft window light.

params.label: Pace
params.effect: Speed of the draw, hold and wipe cycle; 0 freezes the board mid-lesson.

params.label: Mark size
params.effect: Size of the drawn figures against the frame; low is small tidy diagrams, high is a few big sweeping ones.

params.label: Stroke width
params.effect: Width of the chalk line; low is a sharp new stick, high is the flat side of a worn one.

params.label: Dust
params.effect: Strength of the eraser ghosts, wash streaks and settled dust; 0 is a freshly washed board.

params.label: Coloured chalk
params.effect: How much of the drawing uses palette-tinted pastel sticks; 0 is all white chalk.
